solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: No tips for easy life? Pull the other one

indicators.note: losing its tips means each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: easy without its ends gives its middle pair
life without its ends gives its middle pair

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that an easy life comes without perks, telling a friend to pull the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic retorts expressing disbelief at what someone has just claimed.

clue.text: Pioneer at least did this in past — a clever eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historical remark about a pioneering genius whose cleverness made him an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: Pioneer is not a generic trailblazer but NASA's Pioneer probes, which flew out through the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pioneer probes were spacecraft, so voyaging beyond Earth is exactly what they did.

clue.text: Being compatible with drink, supply can in advance

indicators.note: in advance means these come before the drink in the answer

parts.note: to fit out is to supply or equip
a tin is a can
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Instructions for stocking a bar: supply the cans before the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fitting in is in harmony with those around them, suiting the group.

clue.text: Battle soldiers following security into hospital department

indicators.note: into means the following pieces are put inside the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: following means the soldiers come after the security

parts.note: a gage is a pledge given as security
men are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops arriving after the guards burst into a hospital ward, a little skirmish.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a military clash between opposing forces, a fight.

clue.text: Partners beginning to enjoy kiss in part of bay, say?

parts.note: East and West are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of enjoy

parts.note: first letter of enjoy
to neck is to kiss

explanation.surface: Lovers starting to kiss in a secluded part of a bay on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The bay is not a stretch of coast but a bay horse; a ewe-neck is a thin, concave horse's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe-neck is a faulty neck shape found in horses, and a bay is one example of a horse.

clue.text: Suitable time to stop horns in fog being blasted — they're useless

parts.note: good means suitable

indicators.note: to stop means plugging a gap, so the time letter goes inside
being blasted means these letters are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Foghorns are blaring, and someone says it is high time to stop them since they achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-for-nothings are worthless, idle people, plural like the definition.

clue.text: Prattling 80s boy band rocks

parts.note: gab is idle prattling chatter
Bros were a British boy band of the late 1980s

explanation.surface: A chatty 1980s boy band really rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks looks like a verb of praise; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabbro is a dark, coarse-grained igneous stone, so gabbros are kinds of rock.

clue.text: Banish material, two tons of it ditched

indicators.note: ditched means these letters are thrown out of the material word

parts.note: textile is material, cloth
T is the abbreviation for ton, so two of them

explanation.surface: Someone throws away two tons of unwanted cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to expel them from their country, to send them away.

clue.text: Castle not wanting for lock

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without the word for, so it is removed

parts.note: a fortress is a castle

explanation.surface: A castle with no need of a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock suggests a castle door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Boys' Brigade penning song of praise, including most of lad's slogan

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the brigade letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: BB is the abbreviation for the Boys' Brigade, a Christian youth organisation

indicators.note: including means the anthem holds the shortened lad inside it

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youth group sings a hymn containing a boy's motto.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the rallying cry of the nuclear disarmament campaign of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Cardinal in all sections of Voluntary Service Overseas

parts.words: in all sections of Voluntary Service Overseas
parts.note: each of the three words of the charity's name contains a V, the Roman numeral for the number wanted

explanation.surface: A senior churchman involved in every branch of an overseas volunteering charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal is a number, not a churchman; the letter V sits inside each of Voluntary, Service and Overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number is a counting number such as one, two or this one.

clue.text: English father caught turning red

indicators.note: turning means the assembled letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An Englishman, caught out, goes red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a bright cherry shade, so it is a colour in the red family.

clue.text: Permanently go back into splits

indicators.note: into means the turned word goes inside the splits

parts.note: forks are splits or branchings

indicators.note: back means the word for go is read backwards

parts.note: to go is slang for to pee, to urinate

explanation.surface: A dancer resolves to go back into the splits for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the informal sense of relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given for keeps is given for ever, never to be returned.

clue.text: Blab about English vicar after contriving to deceive

indicators.note: about means the blab word goes round the rest

parts.note: to prate is to blab or talk foolishly

indicators.note: after contriving means the vicar's letters have been contrived into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gossip talks about an English vicar after he schemes to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevaricate is to evade the truth, speaking misleadingly.

clue.text: Trace bones, say

parts.note: Bones is Dr McCoy of Star Trek, and a sawbones is a doctor, abbreviated DR
EG (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A forensic note: look for a trace of bones.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreg is a tiny remaining amount, a last vestige of something.

clue.text: Old leader fooling sucker three hours before 10

indicators.note: fooling around with these letters jumbles them

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hour, three times
the answer to 10 across is the number written V in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A former ruler spends three hours tricking a dupe before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is a cross-reference, not ten o'clock: the answer at 10 across, as a Roman numeral, supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964.

clue.text: Cheats hiding name sign nicknames

indicators.note: hiding means the cheats word covers the others inside it

parts.note: to cog is an old word for cheating, especially with loaded dice
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: Swindlers concealing their names behind aliases.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a surname or nickname; the plural fits.

clue.text: Making uniform for date, perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a night out, such as a romantic date

explanation.walkthrough: Uniform reads as clothing; it means level, even.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a verb for smoothing things level and a noun for a social occasion after dark.

clue.text: Small computer secretary has observed outside

indicators.note: has observed outside means the observed word is wrapped around the secretary

parts.note: noted means observed
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary who has spotted a small computer sitting outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a compact portable computer, like a notebook or tablet.

clue.text: Tortuous paths to high-level cover-ups?

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Winding routes leading to scandal concealment at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover-ups suggests scandal; here it is literal: tall hats that cover the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is a tall hat, a head covering that sits high, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Nibble cheek once taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards, so the old word is read in reverse

parts.note: wang is an archaic word for the cheek or jaw

explanation.surface: Someone startled at being nibbled on the cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnaw is to bite at something persistently, chewing at it.

clue.text: Weird church official lacking energy later, and desire

indicators.note: lacking energy later means the later of the official's two energy letters is dropped

parts.note: an elder is an official of some churches
an itch is a desire

explanation.surface: A churchman, drained of energy, later has an odd craving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Later' says which E goes: the second one, leaving ELDR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eldritch means eerie, uncanny and unearthly.

clue.text: Keep, somehow, to sandwich course

indicators.note: to sandwich means these words hold the answer between their outer letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep a sandwich course going somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like a meal's course; it is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a famous racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Remained daily in Berlin — that is to be censored

indicators.note: to be censored means cut out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Die Welt is a Berlin-based daily newspaper
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Berlin newspaper stayed put, though something was censored.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to stay or linger.

clue.text: Using many words and images, keeping part mostly concealed

indicators.note: keeping ... concealed means the images word holds the shortened part hidden inside
concealed completes keeping, the part held out of sight inside

parts.note: pix is informal for pictures, images

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A wordy, illustrated piece that keeps some detail hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix writing is long-winded and verbose.

clue.text: Bring up small seat

parts.note: a pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a small seat to be brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to vomit, a sense of bring up.

clue.text: Time when battery production may be up in the air?

definitions.text: Time when battery production may be up in the air?

parts.words: Time when battery production may be up in the air?
parts.note: battery is a whimsical name for batter-made things, and tossing sends them up in the air on a Shrove Tuesday tradition

explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests electrical cells or hens; read it as what is made from batter, which is tossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday is the British day for making and tossing flat batter cakes.

clue.text: More than one Protestant poet cutting alcohol

indicators.note: cutting means the poet slices into the alcohol word

parts.note: meths is methylated spirits, a form of alcohol
an odist is a writer of odes, a poet

explanation.surface: Several Protestants with a poet making them give up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits Methodist temperance; meths is methylated spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodists belong to a Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley.

clue.text: Middle Eastern city's god coming west

indicators.note: in an across answer coming west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: Zeus is the chief Greek god

explanation.surface: A city's deity travels westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is an Egyptian port at the southern end of the Suez Canal, commonly grouped with the Middle East.
